housing.summary: Amsterdam has an extremely tight and expensive rental market, with high demand and limited supply. Newcomers typically use lettings agencies (makelaars) or online portals; furnished and short-stay options carry a premium. Registration at a rental address is required to obtain a BSN, so a genuine rental contract permitting registration is essential.

banking.summary: Opening a Dutch bank account generally requires a BSN, proof of address, passport/ID and often proof of employment. Major banks offer expat-friendly onboarding; digital banks are common alternatives for arrivals awaiting a BSN. An iDEAL-capable Dutch account is important for everyday payments.

schools.summary: Amsterdam offers Dutch public schools, bilingual (TTO) streams, and several international schools serving expat families. Dutch-subsidised international education and private international schools follow varied curricula; places are limited and waiting lists common, so early application is advised.

legal_admin.summary: New residents must register with the municipality (Gemeente Amsterdam) at their address, which triggers issuance of a BSN. EU/EEA nationals register directly; non-EU nationals typically arrange residence/work authorisation via the IND before or alongside registration. Bring passport, birth certificate (often legalised/translated) and proof of address.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register (inschrijving) in the BRP at Gemeente Amsterdam to obtain a BSN

tax_finance.summary: Income tax and social contributions are administered by the Belastingdienst. Employees are taxed via payroll withholding; the BSN is used for all tax matters. Qualifying skilled migrants may be eligible for the 30% ruling, a significant expat tax advantage that must be applied for.

transport.summary: Amsterdam has an extensive public transport network of trams, buses, metro and ferries operated primarily by GVB, plus national rail (NS). Payment uses the OV-chipkaart or contactless bank card/OVpay. Cycling is a dominant mode of transport across the city.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid; many non-EU licences must be exchanged for a Dutch licence at the RDW/municipality, sometimes requiring a test unless covered by the 30% ruling exchange scheme.
transport.healthcare_registration: Dutch basic health insurance (basisverzekering) is mandatory for residents; register with a private insurer and with a local GP (huisarts).
